fact: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and has almost no atmosphere. Days are scorching and nights are freezing.
Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick carbon dioxide clouds trap heat, hotter than a pizza oven! It also spins backwards compared with most planets.
Earth is the only planet we know of with life. About 71% of its surface is covered by water.
Mars is the Red Planet, coloured by rusty iron dust. It has Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system, and two tiny moons.
Jupiter is the biggest planet, more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it. Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth that has raged for hundreds of years.
Saturn's beautiful rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock. Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub!
Uranus spins on its side, like a rolling ball. It looks blue-green because of methane gas in its atmosphere.
Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and has the fastest winds in the solar system, over 1,000 miles per hour!
The Moon is Earth's only natural moon. Its gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's, and with no wind or rain, astronaut footprints stay there for a very long time.
Ceres is the biggest object in the asteroid belt and a dwarf planet. The Dawn spacecraft found mysterious bright spots on it made of salty minerals.
Europa is an icy moon of Jupiter. Under its frozen crust there may be a huge salty ocean, one of the best places to look for life beyond Earth.
Titan is Saturn's biggest moon. It has a thick orange haze and lakes and rivers of liquid methane and ethane. It is the only moon with a thick atmosphere.
Pluto is a dwarf planet far beyond Neptune. It has a giant heart-shaped glacier, and the New Horizons spacecraft flew past it in 2015.
